methodological_eligibility.evidence_quote: This study presents a comprehensive analysis of 30 research papers that define criteria for evaluating the energy performance of photovoltaic (PV), solar thermal (ST), and hybrid photovoltaic-thermal (PVT) panels in building integration.

stage1.ineligibility_reason: Systematic review of criteria for evaluating the energy performance of solar PV, solar-thermal and hybrid PVT panels in building integration (thermodynamic efficiency, primary-energy, exergy and energy-equivalence metrics for comparing solar-generation technologies). It does not present, characterise, evaluate or critique an EnPI/EnB energy-performance measurement model in the ISO 50001/50006 sense: no energy baseline, no normalised energy-consumption indicator model, and no ISO 50001/50006 engagement. 'Energy performance indicators' appears only as a keyword/incidental term, and the focus is exclusively buildings/solar generation with no industrial component.

paper_type.evidence_quote: To evaluate how existing research compares the energy performance of PV, ST, and PVT technologies through a systematic review

stage1.notes: Ineligible (v2.3): systematic review of solar PV/ST/PVT panel energy-performance evaluation criteria (energy, primary energy, exergy, energy equivalence) in buildings; not an ISO 50001/50006 EnPI/EnB measurement model (EnPI keyword only). level_3b=false: buildings/solar, no continuous-process sector. Eligibility is a judgment call worth human review.
